themes: The hall lantern is a welcome sight after a long walk.
A little firewood keeps my bread oven warm. I can share fresh loaves.
Take my spare rod. There are good fishing waters beyond the valley.
Leave the young trees standing and the forest will always provide.
A well-balanced axe saves your woodcutters a lot of effort. I forge steel and masterwork blades.
I trade woodland berries for firewood.
My spare axe deserves a home with a hardworking woodcutter.
Follow the flowers. The bees know every quiet corner of this meadow.
Take my spare sickle for one of your farmers. A clean cut makes a generous harvest.
My steel and masterwork sickles help farmers bring in more from every harvest.
A spare sickle is a fine way to start a new field.
My hens lay more eggs than I need. Bring wood for their shelter.
Keep water close and watch how the wind shapes the sand.
Take my spare desert outfit, or buy another. Wear it to gather 20% more berries.
A sharp axe is useful even far from the forest. I sell steel and masterwork tools.
Every outcrop tells a story. I am still learning to read this one.
The ridge gets cold at night. I swap vegetables for fuel.
Take my spare swamp boots, or buy another pair. Wear them to reach dark swamp ground and gather 20% more herbs.
Willow roots love the wet ground. Look for herbs among the reeds.
The pools are quiet, but there is plenty of life beneath the lily pads.
I craft steel and masterwork fishing rods for a more generous catch.
Bring firewood and I will share fresh fish from the marsh.

stages.dialogue: A traveler is feverish, and my mentor’s remedy has slipped from memory. Will you help me remember?
Bring three herbs from the patches among the reeds. Their scent may bring the old lesson back. Allocate herb storage in a storehouse before gathering.
Willow, of course! My mentor brewed it gently and always served a meal afterward. Two more herbs and four food will let me care for our visitor.
The traveler is resting comfortably. I remembered the recipe, but you reminded me why my mentor taught it. Keep this leaf from her willow.
My old friend kept a lantern burning for travelers. Her light went dark last winter. Help me prepare to look for her?
Four food will see me through the walk. I will follow the old route and bring back word.
She is safe! Her shelter fell apart, and she moved to stay with family. Let us keep her welcome alive: finish three road tiles in your town and bring six wood for a new lantern shelter.
The shelter has a light again, and your road welcomes weary feet. My friend sent this token: a promise that someone will leave a lantern burning.
I found a carved line beneath the moss on an outcrop. It might be part of a map. Will you help survey the rocks?
Examine three different rock outcrops and return with your notes. Walk beside each rock and select it to record its markings.
The lines join! They mark a doorway beneath the ridge. Bring two wood for charcoal, and I will copy the route for you. We should gather companions before venturing inside.
Here is our map. Gather a companion and open The Sealed Quarry from your You panel. The old gate needs two pairs of hands, and the carvings beyond it may explain what the quarry keepers left behind.
